ModMetaData.name: RimMandrake: Sea Shores
ModMetaData.author: Mandrake
ModMetaData.description:
SEA_FLOOR_AND_CATCH_PASS_1 — makes a MODDED ocean-class biome behave as a real coast for the LAND tiles beside it. The problem this solves is engine-shaped and total. In 1.6 a coastline is the `Coast` tile mutator, and worldgen attaches it only where `World.CoastDirectionAt(tile)` is valid — and that method counts a neighbouring tile as sea ONLY when its PrimaryBiome is the vanilla `Ocean` def, by reference. Any modded ocean biome is invisible to it. A land tile beside one therefore has no coast direction, gets no `Coast` mutator, generates no ocean water and no beach at all, reads `IsCoastal == false` (so no coastal animals, no emerge-from-water arrivals, no river delta), and its water bodies — if any — are Freshwater. Its neighbour's catch table is consulted by nobody, because `WaterBody.SetFishTypes` and `FishingUtility` read only the biome of the MAP THE PAWN STANDS ON. This mod makes a sea opt in with one modExtension on its BiomeDef:
  • ... ...
    • and then, for every land tile bordering it: 1. `IsCoastal` becomes true (Harmony postfix on `World.CoastDirectionAt`, seeded exactly the vanilla way). 2. Worldgen attaches `RM_SeaCoast` instead of vanilla `Coast` (prefix on `WorldGenStep_Mutators.TryAddMutator`), so the shore is laid with the SEA's own deep/shallow terrain and the land biome's beach — scalding shallows for the Scald, solid propane for the Propane Lake. 3. A frozen, hand-authored planet is healed on load: tile mutators are Scribed, so a world that was painted before this mod existed never re-runs worldgen. A WorldComponent adds `RM_SeaCoast` to every qualifying tile that carries no Coast-category mutator yet. Idempotent, and settings-gated as world-affecting. 4. Fishing on that shore pulls the SEA's catch table, not the land biome's (postfix on `WaterBody.SetFishTypes` keyed by the water body's terrain, plus a transpiler swapping the rare-catch table lookup). Nothing here is campaign-specific and nothing here names a biome: a sea is whatever carries the extension. Every behaviour has its own Mod Settings toggle and all-off degrades exactly to vanilla.
